subject.title: [Bug]: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC derivation key

question: Should Mattermost interaction signing move from bot-token-derived secrets to generated or persisted per-account interaction secrets, and what upgrade behavior should existing accounts and external button posters receive?
rationale: The current behavior is a security-sensitive callback-integrity boundary, but it is also documented as the external token-generation contract and may require config or credential-state migration.

options.title: Require migration-backed per-account secrets
options.body: Adopt a per-account generated or configured interaction secret with doctor/config migration, docs updates, and tests proving bot-token-derived forgeries are rejected.

options.title: Accept the existing trust model
options.body: Keep bot-token-derived interaction signing and close the candidate fix only if maintainers decide bot-token possession is already inside the intended Mattermost trust boundary.

options.title: Narrow to operational hardening
options.body: Document stricter deployment guidance or source-IP restrictions without changing token derivation, leaving the core forgery concern unresolved.

recommendation.title: Require migration-backed per-account secrets
recommendation.body: Adopt a per-account generated or configured interaction secret with doctor/config migration, docs updates, and tests proving bot-token-derived forgeries are rejected.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent Mattermost/channel runtime ownership signals and was pulled into the issue timeline, making him the best available decision owner for the security/product boundary choice.
